newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: First Kazakh savings bonds a success, bankers say.
newsitem.headline: First Kazakh savings bonds a success, bankers say.

text.p: Subscriptions for the first National Savings Bonds (NSOs) issued by the Kazakh government for small investors on September 11 ended in a flurry of buying on Friday, and the authorities said the issue was a success.
"The results of the subscription are more than satisfactory and volumes are above all expectations," Roza Akhmetova, head of government securities at Narodny Bank, told Reuters.
A Finance Ministry official said subscription volumes were substantial, but precise figures would only be issued on Monday.

Narodny Bank, formerly the state-owned Sberbank, and Kazkommertsbank, selected by the Finance Ministry as its NSO agents, were allocated 200 million and 100 million tenge of bonds respectively to sell to households.

Once half the the bonds had been sold to private persons, the issue was opened to banks and commercial companies, several of whom rushed in aggressivly to buy paper, said Leila Aliyeva in charge of the Almaty stock centre of Narodny Bank.
The 364-day 1,000-tenge bonds, whose yields are pegged to those on Treasury bills, will pay a coupon of 27.4 percent annual for the first quarter.
Small investors -- mostly pensioners and middle-aged persons seeking to secure their cash saved -- bought most of the issue, Aliyeva said.
NSOs offer better returns than bank accounts where deposits carry fixed interest rates of four to 25 percent annual.
Narodny Bank estimates that Kazakhstan's 17 million people hold about $1 billion in cash, with many preferring to keep their savings under the mattress rather than trust fledgeling financial markets.
